summary: Deliver a client-facing arithmetic calculator service with the four basic operations plus remainder, clear domain errors for invalid uses (especially division or remainder by zero), and a single-slot memory (clear / recall / add / subtract) that starts at zero, with HTTP/API and module surfaces that make these behaviors checkable—without auth, multi-user memory, history, or other product extras.
goal: Clients can perform add, subtract, multiply, divide, and remainder through a checkable service surface; invalid uses fail with a named domain error; a single memory slot supports clear, recall, add-to-memory, and subtract-from-memory starting at zero.
background: This change defines scope for the arithmetic-api evaluation sample. An existing TypeScript HTTP stack may already be present; use it only as implementation context. Scope comes from this brief, not from existing OpenAPI, OCL, or Feature files.
in_scope: Binary arithmetic operations: add, subtract, multiply, divide, and remainder (mod)
Clear, named domain error for invalid uses—especially division by zero and remainder by zero—rather than opaque language/runtime errors
Single-slot calculator memory initialized to zero
Memory operations: clear (set to zero), recall (return current value), add-to-memory, subtract-from-memory
HTTP/API surface that exposes calculate and memory behaviors in a form clients and tests can exercise
Module-level contracts that make the same arithmetic and memory behaviors checkable
out_of_scope: Authentication, authorization, sessions, or API keys
Multi-user or multi-slot memory; per-client isolated memory stores
Operation history, undo/redo, or expression/transcript logging
Scientific, bitwise, or advanced math beyond add/sub/mul/div/remainder
Persistent storage, databases, or durable memory across process restarts (beyond in-process single slot)
UI / frontend clients, SDKs, or third-party integrations beyond the service surface itself
Rate limiting, quotas, observability product features, or multi-tenancy
assumptions: Operands and memory values are numeric (real/number) values suitable for the sample service
Memory is one in-process slot shared by the service instance, not keyed by user or session
Existing TypeScript arithmetic-api layout (HTTP server, OpenAPI/OCL paths) may be reused as stack context without treating current contracts as the source of required scope
constraints: Do not invent product features beyond the stated arithmetic + single-slot memory scope
Domain failures for invalid arithmetic (notably / and remainder by zero) must be named and distinguishable from opaque language errors
ChangeBrief only at this step: no Feature files, WorkPlan, OpenAPI, OCL, tests, or implementation edits as part of brief emission
Contract kind and density choices are deferred to later solidsdd-judge; this brief only requires that HTTP/API and module surfaces remain checkable
success_criteria: A client can request each of add, subtract, multiply, divide, and remainder and receive the correct numeric result for valid inputs
Division by zero and remainder by zero fail with a named domain error observable at the service boundary
Memory starts at zero; clear sets it to zero; recall returns the current value; add-to-memory and subtract-from-memory update the single slot as specified
HTTP/API and module contract surfaces exist such that the arithmetic and memory behaviors above can be verified without relying on opaque implementation internals alone

human_gate.reason: Scope is explicit and additive for a sample calculator service; no blocking ambiguity, auth/money boundary, or conflicting requirements.
